title: H-INV-2: Lineage Forgery Battery — The Crossing Ledger Rejects Every Fabricated History (106/106 Controls Valid, 48/48 Forgeries Rejected)
description:
H-INV-2 — Lineage Forgery Battery: a direct attack on the journaled-crossing invariant. Where the companion SBR-2 exam (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345734) asked whether an adversary can perturb the mesh mid-learning (answer: no), this battery asks whether an adversary can fabricate history the ledger will believe (answer: no).

A 40-epoch bounded training run produced the true crossing journal (2,646 accepted crossings). A preregistered, non-adaptive 6-class forgery battery (8 instances each: orphan weight updates, forged event ids, temporal forgeries, duplicate crossings, orphan healing events, mismatched pattern lineage) fired against the live journal, with 106 legitimate controls audited for lineage completeness.

All 5 falsifiers PASS: 106/106 controls valid with chain intact and bounded-rule recomputation exact; 48/48 forgeries rejected and journaled with zero silent drops; mesh state and journal byte-identical before and after; determinism and append-only held; hygiene clean.

Instrument defects disclosed: two validator defects were caught by the battery's own controls before publication and repaired with the audit/gate validation-mode split; no probe class, falsifier, or acceptance bar changed across repairs; all 48 forgeries were rejected in every version.

Scope honesty: proves THIS registered instrument under THIS frozen battery — not a universal claim about every journal implementation or untested forgery classes. Operator authorization recorded as GO + timestamp per the operator-privacy doctrine.

Dual Mesh Benchmark: MEASURED for the DeepSeek column (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23345241); all other figures NOT MEASURED.

This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.
